title: Justified on-call escalation and temporary root provisioning workflow
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: On-call engineers occasionally need elevated admin privileges to recover production services (investigate KV cache corruption, emergency rollbacks, or manual routing changes). Current ad-hoc methods lack consistent justification, TTL enforcement, and tamper-evident audit trails. We need a repeatable, auditable workflow that grants least-privilege temporary access, tightly scoped to the action, and integrates with RBAC v2, SSO/SAML identity, and our audit pipeline.

Goal: Implement a 'justified escalation' flow for emergency access that: issues time-limited elevated credentials after multi-party approval (or automated risk-based approval for low-risk ops), binds the elevation to a recorded justification and ticket, records cryptographic proof in the audit stream, and automatically rotates/revokes credentials. The flow must be usable by on-call engineers, enforceable by policy, and reviewable by security and compliance teams post-incident.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Temporary elevation can be requested via Console and CLI with a structured justification field and ticket binding (ticket key required).
A2: Every elevation request produces an immutable audit entry containing requester, approver(s), justification, TTL, scoped permissions, and a cryptographic signature/hash.
A3: Elevation credentials have a hard TTL enforced by the token service and cannot be renewed without a fresh request.
A4: RBAC v2 policies are applied at issuance time so the token grants only the minimum necessary permissions for the stated action.
A5: SSO/SAML identity is used as the source of truth for requester identity; MFA requirement enforced for elevated grants.
A6: Standardized post-incident checklist created and attached to each emergency token for follow-up review and audit, including requirement to record commands executed (or session recording link).
A7: Smoke test: simulated recovery by on-call uses the flow end-to-end; audit events surface in the central observability console and are queryable by incident ID.
implementation_steps: Design: finalize escalation approval model (single approver vs dual approver vs automated based on risk scoring). Document trade-offs and UX flows.
API: add /elevation-requests endpoint to token-service with fields {ticket, justification, scope, ttl_secs, approver_required}.
SSO/SAML: enforce assertion binding and require MFA for any elevation request; map SAML roles into RBAC v2 on token issuance.
Token backend: implement short-lived JWT with embedded 'elevation_id' and scope; sign with HSM-backed key and publish signature to audit log stream.
Audit: append an immutable audit record and content-hash to our log store (and mirror to external SIEM).
UI: add Console modal for emergency access request with required fields and visible approver list; surface current active elevations on account page.
Rotation/revoke: implement automatic revoke at TTL expiry and an immediate revoke API for approvers/security; propagate revoke to session manager.
Session capture: integrate with session-recording hooks (where available) or require command logging for manual audits.
Testing: run chaos/recovery drill; verify TTL, RBAC scoping, audit records, and SSO binding under load.
rollout_notes: Phase 1 (design): finalize approval model and RBAC scope templates; security review required.
Phase 2 (backend): token-service changes, audit pipeline extension to include hashes and signatures.
Phase 3 (UI/UX): Console flow and CLI shim; docs and on-call playbook updates.
Phase 4 (pilot): enable for SRE on-call team for 2-week trial and run two recovery drills.
Phase 5 (GA): enable for broader SRE and infra teams; deprecate prior ad-hoc escalation channels.
comments: 2026-03-02 — Lina Chen (SecOps): Prefer HSM-backed signing for audit immutability. Recommend using existing KMS keys and storing signature refs in the audit record.
2026-03-03 — Julian Park (Platform): Need to ensure token-service can handle surge during incidents. Suggest a rate limit bypass for approved on-call requests but with stricter logging.

2026-03-05 — Aisha Patel (creator): Drafted PRD and linked to confluence doc. Added initial approval model: single approver for <30min low-scope ops; dual approver for high-scope. Open to risk-based tweaks.
2026-03-08 — Diego Morales (assignee): Implemented backend prototype for elevation request endpoint; test token issuance and TTL enforcement passing locally. Pushing PR for review.
2026-03-10 — Security review: conditional approval required for provider-involved actions (on-prem operators) and flagged for manual audit.
